archetype.name: Playoff Team (defense-first, short-handed)
archetype.definition: A team coming off a 60-win season that is still winning on defense and ball security, but without its best big it plays more like a good playoff team than the near-elite one it was last year.

report.headline: Still winning, but the Duren-less frontcourt is leaking and November shows it
report.take:
Detroit arrives at 8-4 with a Net Rtg of 5.4, ninth in the league, coming off a 60-22 season in which it ranked second on the site and second in defense. The record is honest. W vs Pt Diff is 0 and the margin implies exactly 8 wins, so nothing here is borrowed from close games. The identity has carried over: a defense ranked sixth (110.3 DRtg), opponents shooting 33.3% from three, the fourth-best Opp TOV % in the league, and its own TOV % eighth. That formula, forcing mistakes and contesting the arc while not giving the ball away, is why this team keeps winning even when it looks thinner than last year.

The thinness is the story. Jalen Duren has played two games, and in those 38 minutes he posted an 8.5 BPM. He is listed out. Without him the frontcourt grades a C against A- groups in the backcourt and on the wing. The damage shows up right where you'd expect. DRB % has fallen to 71.3 (23rd) from 74.2 last season. Opponents are finishing 65.2% at the rim, middle of the pack, after 61.3% a year ago. Opposing power forwards are the soft spot: they score 3.39 points more than their usual output, which ranks 27th, and their rebounding ranks 29th. John Collins carries most of the power-forward minutes with a -4.4 BPM and a -20.9 On-Off. Paul Reed's +15.1 On-Off at center suggests the problem is the four spot more than the five.

The offense is carried by Cade Cunningham, who has 308 points on a 30.3 USG % with a 6.0 BPM, and by Duncan Robinson's shooting: 47 threes at a 65.8 TS %. The team has moved toward the arc, with its 3PA Rate up to 41.7 from 34.5 last season, and it is hitting 36.7%. That works, but Robinson is day-to-day. Cunningham's -8.5 On-Off is the kind of 12-game lineup noise that shouldn't be read as a verdict on him.

The month split is what keeps this from being a comfortable 8-4. October was 5-1 while allowing 101.83 a game. November is 3-3 while allowing 118.67, and the last five games are 2-3 with 124.2 allowed, 13.95 more than the season rate. That includes a 144-140 overtime win at Washington and a 137-point loss at Miami. Some of that is shooting variance, but a defense that can't finish possessions with rebounds will give up more points over time. Until Duren returns, this looks like a top-10 team rather than the top-two side of last spring.

strengths.title: Turnover battle won both ways
strengths.body: Detroit forces turnovers at the fourth-highest rate in the league and protects the ball at the eighth-best rate. Last season's Opp TOV % was 14.8, so this is a carried-over trait rather than a hot start, and it travels against any opponent. It is the most durable part of the profile.

strengths.title: Perimeter defense smothers guards
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 33.3% from three, seventh-best in the league, and opposing point guards and shooting guards produce the fewest combined points, rebounds and assists in the league. Guard length and effort explain this better than shooting luck does, which makes it likelier to last than most early defensive numbers.

strengths.title: Cunningham plus efficient shooting
strengths.body: Cunningham's 6.0 BPM on a 30.3 USG % makes him an engine that holds up under heavy volume. Robinson's 65.8 TS % keeps defenses honest around him. The team's 3P % sits 1.5 points above the league average, which helps cover for fewer easy looks inside.

concerns.title: Frontcourt hole without Duren
concerns.body: With Duren out after two games, Collins and Reed carry the big-man minutes, and opposing power forwards are feasting: their scoring and rebounding above their norms rank among the worst allowed in the league. Defensive rebounding has dropped well below last year's level. This lasts as long as Duren is out.

concerns.title: Defense sliding in November
concerns.body: Points allowed jumped from 101.83 a game in October to 118.67 in November. The last five games run 13.95 worse than the season rate. Some of it is opponent shooting that will settle, but the rim and rebounding numbers say it isn't all noise.

concerns.title: Shooting depends on Robinson's health
concerns.body: Robinson leads the roster in threes and is listed day-to-day. Behind him, Ron Holland's 44.2 TS % and -3.4 BPM is a big drop-off at the wing. If Robinson misses time, the shift toward the arc gets harder to sustain.

trend.note: A 5-1 October built on stifling defense has given way to a .500 November, with the last five at 2-3 and a negative margin. The offense has picked up while the defense has slipped badly.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games, opening against the Spurs on a back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with the hardest test on the schedule: San Antonio is 12-2 with a 13.0 Net Rtg and a top-three defense. The next night brings New Orleans, the league's worst defense, so the back-to-back swings from the toughest matchup to the softest. Toronto at home and a trip to Atlanta round out the week. Both are mid-table sides that force turnovers at elite rates, which tests one of Detroit's core strengths.

A 3-1 week is realistic if the Pelicans and Raptors games go to form. The Spurs game is the one where the frontcourt problem is most likely to cost a result: San Antonio leads the league in rebounds per game and ranks second in DRB %.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's threes vs Spurs' weak spot
keyMatchups.body: San Antonio defends the rim brilliantly but allows 38.2% from three, 28th in the league. Detroit shoots 36.7% from deep, so the path to an upset runs through Robinson and the arc. On the glass, though, the Spurs' 76.5 DRB % will make second chances scarce.

keyMatchups.title: Cunningham against New Orleans
keyMatchups.body: The Pelicans have the league's worst DRtg at 121.2 and let opponents finish 71.4% at the rim. They also give point guards 30.86 points a game, 27th in the league. On the second night of a back-to-back, Cunningham's shot creation should find plenty of room.

keyMatchups.title: Toronto's glass and ball pressure
keyMatchups.body: Toronto ranks fourth in ORB % and first in Opp TOV %. That attacks both Detroit's weak defensive rebounding and its usually clean ball-handling. The Raptors are 5-8, but their -2 W vs Pt Diff says they are better than that record.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Detroit's points allowed come back toward its October level, and whether Robinson plays through his day-to-day tag.

restOfSeason.body: The foundation is real. The record matches the margin, and the turnover edge and perimeter defense are traits this core also showed last season. What won't hold is the October defense, when opponents managed barely over 100 a game. Expect allowed points to settle between that and November's leakier level. Until Duren returns, the team is giving up points on the glass and at the four, which caps it at the edge of the top tier rather than inside it. The current 55-win pace is a little optimistic for a roster that is slipping without its center. Something around 50 wins is the likelier landing spot, with clear upside if Duren comes back healthy and restores last year's interior defense.

confidence.note: Twelve games and a key big out; the core traits match last season.
